claims.statement: AudioPipeline mixes microphone and system audio in fixed windows and fans each mixed window out to two consumers: the recording sender (48 kHz pre-mixed audio for the saved file) and the VAD processor, whose 16 kHz speech segments go to the transcription worker; raw per-device audio is never sent to the recording saver, so the recording contains the mix exactly once.

Two device vocabularies coexist: devices::DeviceType::{Input, Output} identifies physical cpal devices (parsed from names like "... (input)"), while recording_state::DeviceType::{Microphone, System} tags each AudioChunk by its pipeline role, so a physical output device produces System-role chunks.

AudioCapture resamples any device that does not report 48 kHz up to the pipeline's 48 kHz contract at capture time, using a persistent rubato SincFixedIn resampler fed from a fixed 512-sample input buffer; partial remainders are held in the buffer (callback returns early) rather than dropped, and per-chunk resampler creation is avoided because it previously amplified energy (~173% RMS) and produced wrong output sizes.

audio_to_mono averages only the first two channels of multi-channel (mic array) input, because averaging all channels can destructively cancel anti-phase beam-forming auxiliary channels down to near-zero output.

Only microphone audio is enhanced, in a fixed order that matters: high-pass filter at 80 Hz to remove rumble, optional RNNoise suppression (gated by ffmpeg_mixer::RNNOISE_APPLY_ENABLED, default false since Whisper handles noise internally), then EBU R128 loudness normalization to -23 LUFS with true-peak limiting; system audio is captured raw.

AudioMixerRingBuffer mixes in 600 ms windows (the adjacent '50ms' comment is stale) and tolerates up to 8x the window per side (~4.8 s at 48 kHz); a window fires when either side has enough data and a short or empty side is zero-padded instead of last-sample-held; overflow drops the oldest samples after warn (mic) or error (system) logs, and system-audio jitter along the sample-by-sample capture path is the expected cause of residual distortion.

ProfessionalAudioMixer sums mic and system windows and applies proportional soft scaling (a sum exceeding ±1.0 is divided by its own magnitude) instead of hard clamping to avoid 'radio break' artifacts, and applies no post-mix gain because the microphone was already normalized to -23 LUFS at capture (an earlier 2x post-gain caused excessive limiting).

AudioChunk timestamps are recording-relative seconds taken from RecordingState::get_recording_duration; completed VAD speech segments become 16 kHz AudioChunks with timestamp = start_timestamp_ms / 1000.0 so recording-relative timing survives into transcripts, and segments shorter than 800 samples (50 ms at 16 kHz) are dropped both live and at flush.

ContinuousVadProcessor wraps silero_rs, which only runs at 16 kHz (hardcoded VAD_SAMPLE_RATE); the processor internally resamples its 48 kHz input via a moving-average low-pass plus linear interpolation, buffers to 30 ms (480-sample) chunks, and uses thresholds 0.50/0.35, pre/post speech pads of 300/400 ms, and min_speech_time 250 ms so Whisper never receives tiny fragments.

Redemption time is the anti-fragmentation knob: the live pipeline passes 400 ms on all platforms (an earlier cap fragmented 5-second utterances into 40 ms slivers), while batch import and retranscription use VAD_REDEMPTION_TIME_MS = 2000 because whole-file processing would otherwise split speech at every 500 ms-2 s sentence gap; a test asserts 2000 ms yields no more segments than 400 ms and segments stay at least 250 ms.

AudioPipeline::run loops until the channel closes rather than while state.is_recording() (checking the flag previously lost flush signals and buffered chunks during shutdown); chunks with chunk_id >= u64::MAX - 10 are flush signals that trigger flush_remaining_audio, and AudioPipelineManager::force_flush_and_stop sends a burst of such signals with short sleeps to eliminate 30+ second shutdown delays.

AudioPipelineManager::start creates the unbounded AudioChunk channel, installs its sender into RecordingState (captures submit via send_audio_chunk), attaches the recording-saver sender as recording_sender_for_mixed, and spawns the pipeline task; stop() drops the sender to close the channel and awaits the task result.

RecordingManager::start_recording orders the boot sequence as: start RecordingState, detect device kinds for adaptive mixing, set saver device metadata, start the pipeline, sleep 50 ms so the channel is ready, then start the streams and device monitoring; the transcription receiver is returned to recording_commands, which spawns the transcription task for it.

InputDeviceKind classifies inputs as Wired/Bluetooth/Unknown via layered detection (platform-native APIs first: Core Audio transport type on macOS, WASAPI naming on Windows, BlueZ/A2DP/HFP on Linux; then name heuristics; then buffer-size latency >50 ms/<20 ms) and maps to adaptive buffer-timeout ranges of 20-50 ms wired, 80-200 ms Bluetooth, and 80-180 ms Unknown with 2x jitter headroom clamped to the range; kinds are detected per device at start and passed into the pipeline, which currently logs them for monitoring.

FFmpegAudioMixer (exported and unit-tested but not wired into the live mixing path) implements Cap-style adaptive buffering: per-source SourceBuffers become ready when their oldest chunk ages past the device-aware timeout, count gaps (inter-arrival > 2x chunk duration), insert silence on underrun, mix 50 ms windows, and apply RMS-based ducking that reduces system audio to 0.60 gain while mic RMS exceeds 0.01 and runs it at full gain when the mic is silent.

System-audio capture backend is selected via the process-wide BACKEND_CONFIG (AudioCaptureBackend, defaulting to CoreAudio on macOS and ScreenCaptureKit elsewhere, overridden by the persisted system_audio_backend preference); microphones always use CPAL, and a failure to create the system stream is non-fatal — recording continues microphone-only.

The macOS Core Audio backend captures system audio through a mono global process tap in an aggregate device that contains ONLY the tap — an earlier configuration that also listed the output device as a sub-device captured every sample twice and caused echo; samples flow through a 128 KB lock-free ringbuf whose consumer is waker-driven, and 10 consecutive push failures set should_terminate to end the stream under backpressure.

Permissions are trigger-based: microphone permission is provoked by building and playing a throwaway cpal input stream (any failure is read as denied), and macOS Audio Capture (14.4+, required for Core Audio taps) shows its dialog automatically when the tap is created, so check_screen_recording_permission always returns true and trigger_system_audio_permission constructs a CoreAudioCapture to force the prompt; a denied permission yields a tap that streams silence.

With auto_save enabled, RecordingSaver::start_accumulation feeds mixed 48 kHz audio to an IncrementalAudioSaver that encodes a checkpoint every 30 seconds (1,440,000 samples) as audio_chunk_NNN.mp4 via the bundled ffmpeg, bounding memory and enabling crash recovery; auto_save=false discards audio and persists only transcripts/metadata; stop_and_save merges checkpoints into a single 48 kHz mono audio.mp4 and atomically (temp + rename) writes transcripts.json and a completed metadata.json with the actual recording duration.

RecordingState enforces the failure policy: report_error stops recording after 10 recoverable errors, immediately on non-recoverable ones (permission, channel closed, init/config), and after 15 total as a backstop; handle_stream_error classifies cpal errors by message into DeviceDisconnected/PermissionDenied/etc; stop_recording clears the audio sender (closing the pipeline channel) and device Arcs so the microphone is released, and CPAL streams are paused before being dropped so callback Arcs are freed.
Pause is enforced at the state boundary: send_audio_chunk silently discards chunks while is_paused, so capture callbacks keep running without polluting the recording or transcription.

AudioDeviceMonitor polls device enumeration every 2 seconds and emits DeviceDisconnected once when a monitored device is missing for its threshold (3 polls for Bluetooth, which can blip, 2 for wired), DeviceReconnected when it reappears, and DeviceListChanged on list-length changes; events are drained by RecordingManager::poll_device_events and surfaced to the frontend through the poll_audio_device_events command, with attempt_device_reconnect (also a command for a UI Retry button) restarting the matching stream while preserving the other.

On macOS, get_safe_recording_devices_macos evaluates the default microphone and default speaker independently and overrides each Bluetooth device to the corresponding built-in device (when found) because Core Audio/the BT stack resample dynamically and ScreenCaptureKit captures the processed stream, breaking mix sync; the user still hears playback over Bluetooth — only the recording path is rerouted.

Distorted or sped-up review playback through Bluetooth headphones is a playback-side caveat, not a recording defect (BLUETOOTH_PLAYBACK_NOTICE.md): recordings are correct 48 kHz mono files but macOS resampling to a headset's negotiated rate shifts pitch/speed; playback_monitor::get_active_audio_output reports is_bluetooth via per-platform name heuristics over the cpal default output, and the BluetoothPlaybackWarning component polls it every 5 seconds to recommend speakers or wired headphones.

Hot-path logging is optimized: perf_debug!/perf_trace! compile to real log calls in debug builds and to nothing in release, the pipeline logs a summary only every 200 chunks or 60 seconds, per-chunk statistics flow through AudioMetricsBatcher (batches every 50 chunks or 5 seconds into AudioMetricsSummary), and RecordingState owns a 16-buffer AudioBufferPool for allocation reuse.

The transcription task runs a serial worker (NUM_WORKERS=1 to preserve chronological emission) that transcribes each VAD chunk, emits transcript-update events carrying recording-relative audio_start_time/audio_end_time (chunk timestamp plus duration), and verifies zero chunk loss via atomic queued/completed counters during shutdown — waiting without timeout and emitting transcript-chunk-loss-detected if retries cannot reconcile the counts.

Platform enumeration differs: Windows uses the explicit WASAPI host with fallback to the default host and then defaults; macOS lists cpal inputs and outputs but filters the built-in 'speakers' (Bluetooth outputs are allowed); Linux appends ALSA/Pulse 'monitor' sources relabeled as system-audio outputs; and Windows loopback is realized by opening the output device and building an input stream on it, since build_stream always constructs input streams.

Batch VAD entry points (used by audio import and retranscription) process files larger than ~60 s of 16 kHz audio in 10-second chunks with monotonic percentage progress and a cancellation callback that returns an error, and flush() pads the partial buffered chunk with zeros and force-ends any open speech segment so the tail of a meeting is never lost.

The stop sequence stops the device monitor FIRST (continuous WASAPI polling on Windows otherwise prolongs shutdown by 90+ seconds), then stops recording state and streams, force-flushes the pipeline, and calls state.cleanup(); recording_commands drives this via RecordingManager::stop_streams_and_force_flush.
